questions.q: Why does batching requests together to raise throughput create a latency trade-off?
options: Batching has no effect on either latency or throughput in practice
The first request in a batch has to wait for the batch to fill (or the queue delay to expire) before inference runs, delaying its response
Batching only works on CPU, never on GPU
Batching reduces throughput while improving latency
questions.explain: Batching keeps the GPU busier per kernel launch, raising throughput, but the earliest-arriving request in the batch now waits for the batch to fill, which raises its latency.

questions.q: What is the real cost of quantizing a model with torch.quantization.quantize_dynamic?
options: There is no cost; quantization always improves both speed and accuracy
A potential accuracy drop, which is why the original eval harness should be re-run against the quantized artifact before shipping it
The model can no longer be loaded by any serving framework
Quantization only works on models with no linear layers
questions.explain: Reducing numerical precision (e.g. float32 to int8) can reduce accuracy. The guide stresses re-running the eval harness and reporting the accuracy delta, not just the speedup.

questions.q: In a Triton dynamic_batching config with max_queue_delay_microseconds set, what does that setting actually control?
options: The maximum time Triton will wait trying to fill a preferred batch size before running inference anyway
The maximum number of models Triton can serve at once
The total GPU memory allocated to the server
How long a client's HTTP connection stays open
questions.explain: max_queue_delay_microseconds caps how long Triton waits hoping to accumulate a preferred batch size before running inference with whatever has arrived so far.

questions.q: According to the lesson, when is NVIDIA Triton the right serving choice over a plain FastAPI server?
options: Always, regardless of traffic or hardware, because it is newer
Once GPU utilization and multi-model, high-throughput serving actually matter — not before, since FastAPI is faster to stand up for low QPS or early-stage needs
Only when the model was trained in TensorFlow, never PyTorch
Never — Triton cannot serve TorchScript or ONNX models
questions.explain: The lesson frames framework choice as constraint-driven: FastAPI for low QPS or early iteration, TorchServe for PyTorch-native model management, and Triton once GPU throughput and multi-model serving genuinely matter.

questions.q: Why does the lesson emphasize p99 latency over average latency for user-facing systems?
options: p99 latency is always lower than average latency, making the system look better
Average latency can hide a tail of slow requests; p99 captures the latency experienced by the worst 1% of requests, which matters for user experience
p99 latency is only relevant for batch jobs, not real-time systems
p99 latency measures GPU cost, not response time
questions.explain: An average can be dragged down by many fast requests while a meaningful tail is still slow. p99 latency surfaces that tail, which is what users on the unlucky end actually experience.
